1989-2000.what: The two ground-floor sash windows at the left were replaced by a blank shopfront: a wide fascia, a plain panel below it and a projecting sign bracket.
1989-2000.why: Conversion of the ground floor to a shop or other commercial use.

1989-2000.what: The three upper-floor windows were widened from narrow two-pane sashes with heavy trim to wide three-pane windows.
1989-2000.why: Modernisation of the windows for more light; an alteration, not a repair.

2000-2010.what: A balustraded balcony or railing appeared at the left bay, at the left corner of the front.
2000-2010.why: An addition by the owner, probably a balcony or terrace on the bay.

2000-2010.what: The boarded windows (gable window, side windows and the lower window at the front) were opened and glazed again.
2000-2010.why: The house was reoccupied or repaired after standing shut up.

2000-2010.what: All three windows on the lane gable (one in the gable, two below) went from glazed to boarded with braced shutters.
2000-2010.why: The house was vacated or abandoned and closed up.

2010-2020.what: The small extra ground-floor opening beside the door on the long side is no longer there; only the door and lintel remain.
2010-2020.why: Infilled or removed in a small alteration; I could not tell what the opening was.

A.claim: Built as a large, prosperous two-storey timber house with a bay, sash windows and a broad pitched roof; in 1989 its ground floor still had the original sash windows.
Between 1989 and 2000 the ground floor became a shop, with a shopfront fascia and projecting sign.
Between 2000 and 2010 a balcony or railing was added at the left bay.
It stayed well kept throughout: roof, upper windows and walls show no neglect, and the owner kept investing in it.
Before 1989 it was probably a dwelling or a house of some standing that had not yet been converted to trade.

B.claim: Built as a modest two-storey house with small-paned sash windows, window boxes and a door hood on the quay road.
Its upper windows were enlarged between 1989 and 2000 to wide three-pane openings; a modernisation, not a repair.
After that it was unchanged and kept in order through 2020.
Before 1989 it was lived in and kept, with no sign of neglect.

C.claim: In 1989 and 2000 the house stood shut up, with its side, gable and lower windows boarded; it was vacant or let go.
By 2010 it had been reopened and reglazed, so it was reoccupied or repaired, and it stayed so to 2020.
The lower lean-to at the front and the dark open undercroft are present in every year; they look like older alterations.
It probably stood empty for some time before 1989, since it was already boarded then.

D.claim: A small gable-fronted house perched on the rock outcrop above the landing; glazed and apparently occupied in 1989 and 2000.
Between 2000 and 2010 it was closed up, with all lane-side windows boarded, so it was vacated or abandoned.
It stayed boarded and unrepaired through 2020.
Before 1989 it was lived in and kept in order.

E.claim: The small house closing the view up the lane looks essentially unchanged in 1989 to 2020, with glazed windows and no sign of neglect.
An extra opening beside its door on the long side existed in 1989, 2000 and 2010 and was gone by 2020, so there was a small alteration late on.
Before 1989 it was probably a modest dwelling or outbuilding that had been in steady use.
